messages:
maya: heads up — our canary for release/quant-scheduler hit a CI perf regression on x86-int8 pools, latency p50 jumped ~22% after merge rfc/quant-scheduler (seen in gate perf job).
omar: ugh, saw the alert. is this the same batcher change that touched kernel selection heuristics?
liam: probably related. I instrumented a few sample traces — the scheduler is picking a different kernel path for several blocks (uses the dequant-hotpath).
sophia: any KV-cache churn in those traces? iirc earlier regressions were kv thrash related.
liam: kv cache hit-rate is stable, but we see increased dequant time in the decode hotloop. stack traces point to kernel_selector returning `kernel_v2_dequant` vs `kernel_v1_fused` for short-seq (<128) cases.
maya: timeline: merge landed at 2324400000, CI perf regression first observed at 2324450000, canary rollout stopped by ops.
devon: bisect tip: reverting commit 5f3a2f9 (scheduler heuristic tweak) locally restores p50 to baseline on our repro rig.
omar: can you post the perf diff? numbers + flamegraphs pls.
liam: attaching quick summary (p50/p95 tokens/ms).

```
baseline: p50=42ms p95=86ms
post-merge: p50=52ms p95=110ms
revert-5f3a2f9: p50=43ms p95=88ms
```

liam: flamegraph shows a 1.6x larger area in dequant loop for post-merge; kernel_v2_dequant has expensive memory ops in the inner loop.
sophia: kernel_v2 was meant to better support int8 pack formats, but maybe it's mis-selected for profiles where packing cost > dequant cost.
maya: interesting, can we force kernel_v1_fused for affected model in canary to get us back to baseline? that would be a quick mitigation.
devon: yes, I pushed a temporary rollout patch to route model:openint8-7b -> kernel_selector:prefer_fused which dropped p50 back to 44ms on canary. ops unblocked the rollout.
omar: good short-term. longer-term root cause? why did selector prefer kernel_v2_dequant now?
liam: selector change added a heuristic: prefer kernel_v2 when average sequence length < 64 or input is int8-packed. But our telemetry shows sequence lengths skew short during startup ramps, and the selector weights were tuned from an old benchmark (no KV-cache preload).
sophia: so with prefix/KV caching enabled, the actual runtime inner-loop length differs and kernel_v2's memory pattern is worse.
maya: can we update selector to consider kv_cache_hit_rate or prefix_length in decision?
devon: technically yes — add a metric for effective_loop_len = max(seq_len - kv_prefix_len, 1) and use that in kernel scoring.
omar: agree. also add a safety floor: if dequant time delta > 15% in sampling telemetry, prefer fused.
liam: plan: 1) revert heuristic in branch for stable release (short-term). 2) add telemetry counters and sampling profile to gate CI (next). 3) implement effective_loop_len scoring and run scale perf tests.
maya: please file an RFC/PR for the selector change referencing this thread and attach the perf artifacts. Also ping qa for a focused perf job with prefix caching on.
sophia: i can own the perf job. will run 12h sampling across seq dist buckets.
devon: CI bot: perf/regression job 2324509901 failed (p50 delta +22%) — ticket created INF-5143.

ci-bot: [alert] canary rollback prevented (ops hold). Re-run requested after patch.

liam: one more datapoint: quant packing mode 'int8-2b' triggers kernel_v2 more aggressively; we should add a compatibility matrix for packing modes vs kernels. saving that for the PR.
maya: thanks team — nice quick catch. keep updates in this thread and drop links to PR/benchmarks. :thumbsup:
